index.t111: It depends on the risk you choose. The lower the risk per trade, the smaller the position size — and the sooner it runs into the smallest lot the broker allows. What happens next is not what it looks like: the trade still opens, but at the minimum lot, and its risk turns out larger than the one you set. You will think you are risking 0.25%, while on some instruments the risk will be two or three times that.
index.t118:
Gold is the most demanding of all: it has the highest cost per stop,
      so the limit bites there first. For example: on a $1,000 deposit
      at 0.25% risk some instruments will go at an inflated size,
      and on gold the risk will exceed the one set by almost three times.
